max_tire.note: Scout says the platform is 'intended to offer up to 35-inch tires' (Oct 24, 2024). Show concepts have run 35s on 22-in and 18-in beadlock wheels (Traveler) and 37s on 18-in wheels (Terra, LA Auto Show, Nov 2025); those are concepts, not production specs.

timeline.change: Volkswagen Group gains the Scout name when its truck arm Traton completes the purchase of Navistar, International Harvester's successor
May 11: Volkswagen approves an independent US company to build electric off-roaders under the Scout name. Sept 1: Scott Keogh leaves Volkswagen of America to become Scout's CEO
March 3: Scout announces a $2 billion plant in Blythewood, South Carolina, able to build 200,000 vehicles a year

Oct 24: Traveler SUV and Terra pickup revealed near Nashville as production-intent concepts, battery-electric or with the 'Harvester' gas range extender. Reservations open; initial production targeted for 2027

January: more than 50,000 reservations, about 70% for the Traveler and more than half for the Harvester range extender (per Keogh). Nov 12: headquarters to move to Charlotte, NC. Nov 18: first auto-show appearance (Los Angeles), quoting retail prices 'starting under $60,000'
Sept 2: Scout says validation vehicles are being built in Blythewood in 2026, continuing into 2027, and that customer deliveries are expected to begin in 2028
